speaker: Doctor
text:
I notice you mentioned a neck swelling, but I haven't received your symptoms yet. To start our evaluation, how long have you had this swelling, and has it been growing rapidly or slowly?

REQUEST TEST: Thyroid_Functions, CBC, TSH, T3, T4, and Thyroid_Antibodies.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the results; since your thyroid function is normal, is the swelling painful, and does it change in size when you swallow or move your neck? REQUEST IMAGES: Neck_Ultrasound

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a progressively increasing swelling on the nape of his neck for 2 months. He denies having a fever, pain, or any discharge from the swelling. He mentions a history of colon cancer for which he underwent colectomy at the age of 43. He also has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and osteoarthritis of the left knee. He takes insulin glargine, metformin, enalapril, and naproxen.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of colon cancer and the progressive, painless swelling, I need to check if this is a metastatic lymph node. Has this swelling ever been biopsied or imaged previously, and does it move when you swallow? REQUEST IMAGES: Neck_Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Metastatic lymphadenopathy from recurrent colon cancer. The normal thyroid function rules out primary thyroid disease, and the progressive, painless swelling in a patient with prior colon cancer is highly suggestive of metastasis.
